title: Haven't You Heard? I'm Sakamoto
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: First-year student Sakamoto is impossibly cool: girls adore him and many boys resent him. Whatever pranks, bullying or traps classmates throw at him, he turns them aside with absurd grace, and he quietly helps people who ask, including Kubota, who is being bullied for money until Sakamoto helps him find a part-time job and stand up for himself. Former bullies come to admire him, and the series ends with Sakamoto leaving for America to pursue becoming an astronaut (Wikipedia; Seven Seas blurb; AniList Surreal Comedy, Episodic).
life_message: Meeting hostility with composure, kindness and style can change the people around you.

content.note: Delinquents and pranks aimed at Sakamoto; slapstick confrontations (AniList Delinquents; MU Delinquent/s).
Girls' admiration of Sakamoto; no romance arc noted.
A delinquent gives up smoking for blowing bubbles after meeting Sakamoto (Wikipedia).
Kubota bullied for money, later has his hair shaved off by delinquents and hides in his room; pranks aimed at Sakamoto (Wikipedia; Seven Seas blurb; AniList and MU Bullying).
Pranks and traps set by classmates; Sakamoto's stunts (to verify).

dominant: Stoic composure; virtue through example; absurdist comedy

frames.aligns: Sakamoto answers malice with patience and helps the bullied boy, close to turning the other cheek.
frames.concerns: Pride in coolness could be read as vanity.

frames.aligns: Dispassion in the face of provocation.
Overcoming evil with good (Romans 12:21) toward bullies.
Common-grace picture of patience and integrity.
Doing good to all, including enemies.
Gentle satire with a moral center.
Equanimity like the Gita's steady-minded person.
Non-reactive calm and compassion toward tormentors.
Harm none, even to those who intend harm.

frames.concerns: Turning the other cheek sits apart from proportionate retaliation.

frames.aligns: Guarded speech and chesed to the bullied.
Kindness; no lashon hara from the hero.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Sakamoto never retaliates against insults or traps; dignity is inner.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Helps any classmate who asks, including the bullied boy.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Flamboyant personal style is the whole premise.

folkways.japan: The gakuran-uniform school, delinquent cliques and the pressure to conform form the backdrop Sakamoto's individuality plays against.

delivery.evidence: Gag comedy where Sakamoto's example, not speeches, wins people over (Wikipedia; Seven Seas blurb) (to verify).
delivery.note: Antagonists are mocked but also redeemed and shielded, so they are not purely foolish.

winners_losers: Sakamoto always prevails and wins over his antagonists, even shielding a former bully from punishment; bullies are made foolish. Sympathy goes to composure and kindness.
